proposal.hypothesis: For large n, a default-stream memset followed by one CTA-local reduction and one atomicAdd per CTA may avoid the baseline's multiple reduction launches and final copy. Larger CTA tiles reduce the number of contending atomics but increase per-CTA input work. The non-atomic control shares the tiled first-pass kernel structure; performance remains unmeasured and may regress due to memset or atomic contention.

retained: Added one templated CTA-local tiled reduction kernel with compile-time tile sizes and a compile-time choice between one atomic contribution per CTA and one partial per CTA.
For n >= 1024, zeroed the output with cudaMemsetAsync on the default stream and launched the atomic path; selected 128-, 512-, or 2048-element CTA tiles based on input scale.
Added a non-atomic first-pass plus finalization control for n < 1024, using the same 128-element first-pass mapping as the smallest atomic configuration.
Handled n <= 0 by zeroing the output and n == 1 by copying the sole input value; all reduction loads are tail-guarded and no new allocations or stale scratch values are used.
